Document Name.description:
Construct the **Document Name** from metadata in the document.

Format: "(artist_name) - (project_or_song_name) (execution_status)"
- Use project name if present; otherwise use song title(s).
- Multiple songs: comma-separate them.
- Execution status: FX (Fully-Executed), PX (Partially-Executed), NX (No Execution).

Return a single constructed string, e.g. "Drake - Certified Lover Boy FX".

Execution Status.description:
Determine the **Execution Status** by analyzing the signature section.

- All parties signed → "FX"
- Client signed but counterparty did not → "PX"
- Counterparty signed but client did not → "PX"
- No signatures found → "NX"

Return only: "FX", "PX", or "NX".

Song Title.description:
Extract the **Song Title(s)** from the agreement.

Locations: first 1-3 paragraphs ("master recording entitled '...'"), schedules, appendices, or tables ("Schedule A", "List of Masters").

Return ONLY the title(s) — not surrounding phrases. Multiple titles: comma-separate them.

Artist Name.description:
Extract the **Artist Name**. Found in the first paragraph, immediately followed by ("Artist") or similar label.

Return ONLY the name — no quotes, labels, or legal names.

Single/Multisong Line.description:
Extract the **scope phrase** from the first two paragraphs indicating whether this is a single-song, multi-song, or project agreement.

Examples: "one (1) master recording", "multiple master recordings", "an album entitled 'XYZ'".

Client Party.description:
Extract the **Client Party** name — the individual or entity addressed as "you" or "Producer" in the opening paragraph.

Return ONLY the name.

Direct Counterparty.description:
Extract the **Direct Counterparty** — the party issuing the agreement, referred to as "we", "us", or "Company" in the opening paragraphs.

Return ONLY the entity name.

Alternative Counterparties.description:
Extract names of any **Alternative Counterparties** — other entities involved (labels, distributors, licensees) beyond the direct counterparty.

Found in rights assignment clauses, revenue flow sections, SoundExchange LOD, Schedule A, or signature blocks.

Return a comma-separated list of entity names, or "not found".

Classification of Recoupment Language.description:
Extract the **recoupment clause** — the language defining when the Producer becomes eligible for royalty payments.

Look for: "No royalty shall be payable until...", "After recoupment of Recording Costs...", "retroactively from record one after...".

Return the full verbatim sentence(s) explaining the recoupment mechanism.

Effective Date.description:
Extract the **Effective Date** from the first paragraph.

If multiple dates on page 1, select the one labeled "Effective as of..." or "Effective Date:".

Return ONLY the date string.

Distributor.description:
Extract the **Distributor** name.

Look for: "distributed by [Entity]", "released by [Entity]", or "[Entity], a division of [Parent]".

If not explicitly stated, the Label and Distributor may be the same entity.

Return ONLY the entity name.

Label.description:
Extract the **parent company** that owns or controls the label in this agreement.

Look for: "[Label], a division of [Parent]", "owned by", "an imprint of", "subsidiary of".

Return ONLY the parent company name (e.g. "Warner Music Group", "Sony Music Entertainment").

Lawyer Information.description:
Extract **Lawyer Information** for both parties.

Look for: "C/O [Firm]", "represented by [Name]", address blocks near party names.

Return as: {"client_lawyer": "Name, Firm, Address", "counterparty_lawyer": "Name, Firm, Address"}.

Assign based on proximity to the Client Party / Producer name, or explicit labels like "Label's counsel".

Producer Royalty Points.description:
Extract the **initial/base Producer Royalty rate(s)** — one entry per base rate.

IMPORTANT: Only the INITIAL rate. Escalated/bump rates belong in **Bumps**. If "1.5% escalating to 2.0% after Gold", only return "1.5%" here.

Return each rate as a SHORT value (e.g. "3%", "2.8% of NAR"). Do NOT combine multiple rates into one string.

Type of Royalty.description:
Determine the **royalty calculation basis**. Only two valid values:

- "NAR" — Net Artist Rate/Royalties (producer gets % of artist's royalties)
- "PPD" — Published Price to Dealers (producer gets % of wholesale price)

Look for explicit mentions of "net artist royalties/rate" (→ NAR) or "PPD"/"Published Price to Dealers" (→ PPD).

Return "NAR", "PPD", or "not found". Do not guess.

Third Party Money.description:
Extract **Third Party Money** directives from the SoundExchange LOD section.

Return each as a SHORT value — just the amount/percentage (e.g. "9.47%", "$1,500"). Do NOT include surrounding context.

Organization Counting Units.description:
Check if the contract uses **USNRC** (U.S. Normal Retail Channels) for measuring sales.

Look for: "USNRC Net Sales", "Net Sales (USNRC)", "sales through U.S. Normal Retail Channels".

Return "USNRC" or "not found".

Producer Advance Legal Recoupment.description:
Extract the **Producer Advance amount** — the dollar value only.

Look near: "Producer Advance", "Advance payable to Producer", "Advance of $X".

Return ONLY the monetary value (e.g. "$10,000").

Recoupment Classification.description:
Extract the **Recoupment Classification** — how the advance is recouped.

Valid values: "non-returnable recoupable", "partially-recoupable", "fully-recoupable".

Found adjacent to the advance amount. Return ONLY one of the three values above, or "not found".

Legal Advance.description:
Extract the **Legal Advance** amount — the dollar value paid for legal fees.

Look near: "legal advance", "advance for legal fees", "contribution toward legal costs".

Return ONLY the monetary value (e.g. "$5,000").

Bumps.description:
Extract the **royalty escalation clause (Bumps)** — conditional increases above the base rate.

A bump always has BOTH an escalated rate AND a trigger condition. Do NOT include the initial/base rate (that's in Producer Royalty Points).

Return the verbatim escalation clause, e.g. "escalating to 2.0% NAR after RIAA Gold, 2.5% after Platinum".
